issues: Missing alternative text for image elements causes serious accessibility failures. In `expo-app/src/components/ui/EmptyState.tsx` (line 6-10) the <Image> component does not provide an appropriate alt attribute for the web export, resulting in a <div role="img"> without a title or aria-label. Similarly, in `expo-app/src/screens/ReceiptCaptureScreen.tsx` (line ~129) the <Image> component lacks an explicit alt attribute for the web build, causing <div role="img"> elements with no accessible text. The static accessibility check flags these as serious issues. Add proper alt text (e.g., using the `accessibilityLabel` prop and ensuring `accessible={true}`) or provide a `title` attribute so that the rendered HTML includes an accessible description for each image.

Ensure that all `<Image>` components used in the app set `accessible={true}` and a non‑empty `accessibilityLabel` (or `accessibilityHint`) that will be translated to an `alt` attribute in the web build. For example, update the EmptyState image to `<Image source={...} style={...} accessible={true} accessibilityLabel="Empty state illustration" />` and the receipt photo image to include `accessible={true}` and a descriptive `accessibilityLabel` such as "Receipt photo".
feedback: All unit and integration tests pass, but the static validation fails due to serious accessibility violations. Provide descriptive alt text for all image elements to resolve the role-img-alt errors.
